lede: A fast-growing, design-led supplier to India's biggest jewellery chains that has finally started generating cash. Execution on promises is strong. The price already assumes most of the FY30 plan comes true, while most of today's growth comes from the gold price rather than volume.

short_version.text: Revenue up 8x in four years (₹786 Cr → ₹6,295 Cr), EBITDA margin from 2.6% to 7%, ROCE 27%. Most promises from the last two calls were kept or beaten, and operating cash flow turned positive in Q1 FY27 (₹30 Cr), a quarter early.

Q1 revenue grew 78% but volumes only 7–9%; the rest is the gold price. Five years of profit (₹491 Cr) went entirely into working capital. The previous auditor resigned mid-year, and a ₹10.7 Cr fund-diversion incident surfaced in July.
38x trailing earnings for a 4.5% net-margin business; listed B2B peers trade at 13–17x. On management's FY30 profit target the stock is on about 14x, so the upside depends on that target being met.

blocks.text: Sky Gold designs and makes lightweight gold jewellery (mainly cast 22 kt, increasingly 18/14/9 kt and diamond-studded) for retail chains, with no shops of its own. It works as a co-creation partner: it studies a retailer's product mix, designs collections and supplies them. Customers include Malabar, Kalyan, Joyalukkas, Titan, CaratLane, Reliance Jewels, Senco, Aditya Birla, Thangamayil, PN Gadgil, Lalithaa and Damas (Dubai).

items.text: 22 kt plain gold earns a 5–5.5% gross margin; CZ-studded 22 kt lifts it to 6–6.5%.
Lower-karat pieces (14% of volume) add about 1.4–1.5 points of gross margin; studded jewellery (2% of sales) about 0.3.
Advanced gold books only the making charge as revenue: about 1 point of gross margin, no working capital, less interest.
Gold is hedged on MCX (about 99%), so it earns a making margin, not a gold-price bet.

From a Zaveri Bazar workshop (2005) to a 1.5 lakh sq ft Navi Mumbai plant plus acquired units: Sparkling Chains and Starmangalsutra (₹88 Cr, FY25), Speed Bangle (paid in shares at ₹369), 51% of Shri Rishabh Gold.
From cash-hungry growth to 'Sky Gold 3.0': growth capped at 30–35% a year so it can be self-funded, net debt-free by FY30.
Shift to lower karat, studded jewellery and exports; a professional CEO (Akash Talesara) and CFO.

items.lead: Growth is real, but less of it is volume than revenue suggests.
items.text: In Q1 FY27 revenue rose 78% while volumes rose 7–9%. With gold hedged, margins hold in percent, but absolute profit rises and falls with the gold price. Volume guidance was dropped in May.

items.lead: Cash conversion has been the weak spot.
items.text: Five-year net profit of ₹491 Cr went entirely into working capital (operating cash flow –₹489 Cr). Growth was funded by about ₹650 Cr of new equity (cash raises and share-swap acquisitions) and debt, which rose from ₹92 Cr to ₹869 Cr.
Borrowings/equity fell from 1.49x to 0.72x and interest cover rose to 5.8x. Net debt ₹540 Cr at June 2026; target to halve it in FY27 and be net debt-free by FY30.
Capital employed rose ₹1,494 Cr from FY24 to FY26 while after-tax operating profit rose about ₹282 Cr: good, but below the 27% headline ROCE because acquisitions and land used new capital.

items.text: Promoter stake fell from 73.6% (2023) to 51.7% (Jun 2026), mostly through new share issues for fund-raising and share-swap acquisitions.
Domestic institutions went from 0% to 14.2%, foreign from 0% to 2.8%.

The previous statutory auditor resigned mid-year; the 'upgrade to a global auditor' framing leaves this out.
Standalone sales to related parties rose from nil to 4.7% of sales, most likely to its own subsidiaries such as the Dubai arm. Worth confirming.
The annual report's net debt subtracts 'equity shares pledged' (₹44 Cr), a non-standard definition.

Positives: BDO as auditor, zero promoter salary, no gold-metal-loan exposure, 99% hedging.

blocks.text: The stock is up 185% in a year and has re-rated from a small-cap manufacturer to a retailer-like multiple. Real changes support part of that: cash flow turning positive, debt falling, a better auditor and professional management. But the price already pays for the FY30 plan, and the base case gives only mid-single-digit yearly returns, so the margin of safety is thin. Historical average multiples aren't included yet.
